messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: log minimization checklist & sample scrub request

Hi Samira —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and the specific asks we agreed on so we don’t lose momentum. I’ve split items into Security/Engineering asks and timeline.

Security asks (what HealthSync asked Redwood to confirm):
- Can request/response logs be configured to redact sensitive fields (PHI/SSN/contact info) at capture time vs post-ingest? You asked for options and tradeoffs.
- Can trace IDs and header values that might link to internal IDs be hashed or dropped?
- Minimum retention we can support for raw traces and for scrubbed logs.
- Evidence we support tenant residency (US-East only for this POC) and relevant SOC2 controls for logging.

Engineering asks (what we promised to provide):
- A short checklist for log minimization patterns (config flags, recommended scrub pipeline).
- A sample of API request/response logs with PHI redacted the way we propose (anonymized + suffix-hashed trace IDs). You requested sample output you can run through your internal compliance check.
- Pilot scope: 2 endpoints, 72h ingest window, push to our dedicated pilot cluster in us-east.

Next steps / timeline:
1) I’ll share the minimization checklist and a one-page tradeoff table (today EOD).
2) Marissa will produce a small zip with 3 scrubbed sample bursts (no raw PHI) and a README describing transformations (tomorrow AM).
3) Security team to confirm acceptance criteria; we will ship a short technical runbook and SOC2 references (by Fri 6/23).

Attachments: POC-data-proposal.pdf (outlines pilot sizing & success metrics).

Please confirm if we should include additional logging artifacts (e.g., full HTTP headers sample vs header subset). Happy to jump on a follow-up call with Marissa and your security lead if helpful.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: POC-data-proposal.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]

Subject: Re: Post-call: log minimization checklist & sample scrub request

Thanks Priyom — good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side before Marissa prepares the samples: 

1) Redaction vs pseudonymization: our compliance team prefers pseudonymization (reversible under strict control) for traceability across systems; however, for the initial POC they would accept irreversible hashing of identifiers as long as we document key management. Can you include both hashed and pseudonymized examples and note which requires KMS/HSM?

2) Headers: please include full header sets in one sample burst (we will scrub certs/keys locally) and a second sample with header subset (only accept-language, user-agent, x-request-id) so we can validate policy decisions.

3) Retention: can Redwood enforce a 7-day rolling window for raw logs and a 90-day window for scrubbed telemetry? If not exact, please state nearest supported options and whether we can configure per-customer retention.

4) Residency: confirmed — POC must run in us-east and logs must not leave that region.

Also want to ensure we get a simple acceptance checklist for Security to sign off on the pilot (will review once we get your materials).

Samira Khan
Director of Product Security, HealthSync
security@healthsync.com

Hi Samira —

Appreciate the clarifying points. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

1) Hash vs pseudonymize: we will provide two variants in the sample bundle. Variant A = irreversible SHA-256 with truncated suffix for trace ids (non-reversible). Variant B = pseudonymized id mapping with a KMS-backed wrap key; demo will include mapping metadata (not raw keys). Note: pseudonymization requires a managed key; we can run it in your tenant or via Redwood’s HSM if you prefer.

2) Headers: will include two sample bursts as requested — full-headers (sanitized) + header-subset variant. We will strip certs and auth tokens but keep non-sensitive headers for routing analytics.

3) Retention: Redwood supports per-customer retention configuration on Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we can do configurable windows via retention policies; nearest defaults are 7 days (raw) and 90 days (scrubbed) and we can document the configuration steps in the runbook.

4) Residency: confirmed — POC cluster will be pinned to us-east-1 and logs will not replicate outside that region. We will include an audit snippet showing region lock for the pilot.

Planned deliverables (tomorrow AM unless I hear changes):
- Minimization checklist (one page) with recommended flags and sample regexes for common PHI fields.
- ZIP with 3 scrubbed sample bursts (full-headers, header-subset, pseudonymized mapping). File: sample-scrubbed-logs-20280621.zip
- Short runbook + SOC2 control references (log access, key management).

Marissa — can you attach the sample zip and a README describing the transform steps? Also flag any engineering constraints we should surface to HealthSync (e.g., performance impact of synchronous redaction).

Samira — if that timeline looks good I’ll follow-up with a DocuSign NDA for the sample exchange (should be quick).

Thanks,
Priyom
